newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cricket umpire says his style is natural.
newsitem.headline: Cricket umpire says his style is natural.

text.p: WELLINGTON, April 1 - Colourful Auckland umpire Brent Bowden will tone down some of his umpiring signalling extravagances, but will not put them completely out of sight, NZPA reported on Tuesday.
New Zealand Cricket Umpires' Association chairman Brian Aldridge spoke to Bowden about some of his elaborate signalling, asking him to tone it down, especially in longer forms of the game.
Aldridge said some concerns had been expressed by fellow umpires at Bowden's approach and he had agreed to modify some signals.
Bowden, who is umpiring the Shell Trophy final in Christchurch, said:
"I've got a lot of respect for Brian and he has been a mentor for me and helped me with a lot of things.
"I have had a lot of opinions on my style and it is a case of balancing them.
"Nothing really upsets me. What I am doing is natural. I am a bit of an extrovert and I'm not being a show pony."
Bowden said there was a difference between first-class matches and one-day games.
Ten years ago coloured clothing, music and crowd participation were not part of cricket, he said.
"It is a sign of the times. Cricket is changing and I like to think an umpire can show character and flair.
"I like to enjoy myself and I love umpiring in this great game.
"As long as I get my ins and outs right and have the respect of the players and my fellow umpires, that is the main thing.
"I will tone it down for the longer games because the excitement and buzz is not there compared with the one-day games.
"What you see with me is what you get," he said.
Bowden said he was not affected by English media criticism of his style while umpiring during the BNZ Cup one-day series game between New Zealand and England at Auckland last month.
